text:
The Canadiens have points in 11 straight games, 8-0-3, and sit 11-3-4. It's a heater, and it comes with a footnote we'd be wrong to skip: Montreal got exactly half of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that run, and 49% on the season. Our numbers say they deserved about 19 points; they have 26. That is the biggest gap in this group in the good direction.

Some of it is real skill. Cole Caufield is on pace for another 50-goal season, and the top line with Nick Suzuki and Juraj Slafkovsky gets 62% of the chances. Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson drive play from the back. Jacob Fowler has stopped .925 over his last five starts.

The rest is the kind of luck that runs out. The Kaiden Guhle and Alexandre Carrier pair gets only 42% of the chances, and the Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Alex Newhook line gets 39%. Montreal takes about a penalty a game more than it draws, which is a habit that costs points in March.

The room has had a lively week: a heated game with Toronto, Arber Xhekaj promising he'll remember what happened to Kirby Dach, and questions over when Ivan Demidov returns. The playoff odds are 68% in our simulations. What to watch: whether the chance share climbs once Demidov is back. If it doesn't, the streak will end the way most of them do.
headline: Montreal keeps winning the close ones
